newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil net drops after $11.7 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil net drops after $11.7 million charge.

text.p: Pennzoil Co. said Monday that its profits slipped in the second quarter after it took $11.7 million in charges.
The Houston-based oil company said net income for the three months ended June 30 fell by 2.4 percent to $23.9 million, or 51 cents a share, from $24.5 million, or 53 cents a share.
Pennzoil said its revenues grew 2 percent to $648.4 million from $636.6 million, although oil and gas revenues were virtually flat.

However, the company said income from continuing operations increased 44 percent to $35.6 million, or 76 cents a share, with all its business segments improving their operating income. It was the seventh consecutive quarter of year-over-year increases in earnings from continuing operations, the company said.
The Wall Street consensus estimate had been for the company to earn 69 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.

Pennzoil said the $11.7 million in charges were related to the sale of its PennUnion natural gas marketing unit, paying down debt, and costs connected with Union Pacific Resources Inc.'s unsolicited tender offer.
The company said cash flow from operations increased 12 percent to $132.4 million, or $2.82 a share, from $118.3 million, or $2.55 a share.
Pennzoil said its oil and gas division operating income rose 5 percent to $69.1 million from $65.5 million.

The company attributed the rise to higher natural gas prices and lower general and administrative expenses and taxes, which were partially offset by lower production and higher depreciation rates and operating expenses.
Oil production decreased to 62,781 barrels a day from 65,009 bpd. Production rose about 5 percent, excluding the 11,200 bpd output net to Canadian properties that Pennzoil sold last July.
The company's motor oil and refined products division's operating income jumped 63 percent to $25.8 million from $15.8 million.
Pennzoil ascribed the rise to higher margins resulting from upgrading its Shreveport refinery and higher income from its Excel Paralubes joint venture.
Pennzoil said operating income from its Jiffy Lube International Inc. franchises increased 19 percent to $6.3 million in the quarter, mainly due to lower expenses at company-operated stores.
For the first half of 1997, Pennzoil said its net income more than doubled to $81.4 million, or $1.74 a share, from $40.3 million, or 87 cents a sharer.
Revenues in the first half expanded to $1.3 billion from $1.2 billion, with oil and gas revenues increasing 14 percent.
On a recurring basis, first-half earnings improved by 118 percent to $95.7 million, or $2.04 a share, from $43.8 million, or 95 cents a share.
Cash flow from operations in the half increased 26 percent to $279 million, or $5.95 a share, from $221.5 million, or $4.77 a share.
The company's stock lost 25 cents to $77.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
